correctness.rationale: The squared two-step map for pair (i,j) is (a_i^T a_j)^2 P_i because the complementary projections are rank one in the plane. Pay at least q_i per conditional successor (q_0=u, q_±=q=min(u,(2u−1)^2)); taking the two coordinate diagonals gives a lower bound max{q(1−u)(1−t), u t+qu(1−t)}, t=Pr(I=0), for every joint law. Balanced leaves and minimizing successors attain it. For u<1/2 the unique crossing gives the stated t and an isotropic optimal matrix; imbalance already raises the maximum eigenvalue of the cheaper matrix, while at balance any nonzero positive-semidefinite excess strictly increases it. For u>1/2 the vertical quadratic form forces t=0 and minimum successors, and any nonzero off-diagonal entry makes the optimum impossible. At u=1/2 the only zero-overlap pairs are the two opposite-leaf pairs, with arbitrary mixture. The identity (2u−1)^2−u=(4u−1)(u−1) gives the tie at 1/4. The exact benchmarks 3/80 vs 1/16 and 3/16 vs 11/18 follow from the same matrix. An independent diagonal density-matrix dual attains the bound: for u<1/2 its first diagonal is u(1−q)/(u+q(1−2u)), otherwise use the vertical unit projector. That dual and all nine supported/forbidden pair costs were checked at 102 exact rational parameters in /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py (kaczmarz); the grid is corroboration only.
residual_risks: Only a fixed law for a single batch of two unrelaxed projections in the stated symmetric real planar family; not residual-adaptive, IID-constrained, or an asymptotic rate.

value.rationale: A complete shortest-horizon benchmark on a natural symmetric overdetermined geometry separates local successor preference from global balancing of error directions. The exact 3/8 example shows that deliberately including a less favorable pair can improve minimax retention over every deterministic schedule. The two distinct changes in support and the classification of all ties make the result useful for comparisons with independent and coupled designs, without an extrapolation to runtime or long-run rates.
residual_risks: The usefulness is as an exact two-update benchmark, not a performance claim for arbitrary matrices.
